references.text: The psalmist meditates (שׂיח, the same Hebrew root as in Gen 24:63) on God's works, a direct linguistic parallel to Isaac's meditation in the field.
To ponder (הגה/שׂיח) on God's works is a recurring biblical theme that reflects Isaac's evening meditation.
The righteous person's meditation on the Lord's law day and night, a parallel to Isaac's devout practice of going out to meditate.
The psalmist's habit of watching at night to meditate on God's word reflects the same devotion as Isaac's evening meditation in the field.
The outcome of the event in verse 63 – Isaac brings Rebekah into his mother's tent, marries her, and finds comfort after his mother's death.
Isaac lives at Beer-Lahai-Roi, the same area he came from when he went out to meditate (cf. Gen 24:62).
